name: Adaptive Technical Assessment - API Designer
description: Adaptive assessment question bank for API Designer skills. Each question is hand-crafted with diverse formats: scenario, architectural_trade_off, design_review, code_review, governance_case_study, comparison, and debugging. Questions focus on organizational API governance and strategic design — not individual service implementation.

api_fundamentals_http.http_methods_seman.question: Your organization's payment API uses POST /payments for creating payments and POST /payments/{id}/refund for refunding. A new team wants to use DELETE /payments/{id} instead of the refund endpoint. As the API designer, explain why DELETE is semantically incorrect here and what HTTP method governance rule you would add to the organization's API style guide.

api_fundamentals_http.status_code_taxono.question: During an API design review, you find that a team returns HTTP 200 with {"error": true, "message": "User not found"} instead of 404. Another team returns 500 for all validation errors. Draft a status code policy section for the API style guide that prevents these anti-patterns, covering 2xx, 4xx, and 5xx usage rules.

api_fundamentals_http.uri_design_princip.question: A team submits an API design with these endpoints: GET /getUsers, POST /createUser, PUT /api/v1/Users/{userId}/updateProfile, DELETE /remove-user?id=123. Identify all URI design violations and rewrite them following a consistent URI naming standard.
expected_answer_keywords: path params not query for identity

api_fundamentals_http.content_negotiatio.question: Your API platform needs to support JSON and Protocol Buffers responses for different consumer types (web apps vs internal microservices). Design a content negotiation strategy using Accept headers, including how to handle unsupported media types and how to version content formats using vendor media types (e.g., application/vnd.company.v2+json).

api_fundamentals_http.caching_headers_et.question: An API serving product catalog data (updated hourly) and user profile data (updated on write) needs a platform-wide caching directive standard. Define Cache-Control and ETag policies for both resource types, explaining when to use max-age vs no-cache with conditional requests (If-None-Match).

api_fundamentals_http.idempotency_safety.question: Your payment API experiences duplicate charges when mobile clients retry failed POST /charges requests due to network timeouts. Design an organization-wide Idempotency-Key header standard: specify the header format, server-side storage requirements, response behavior for duplicate keys, and expiration policy.

api_fundamentals_http.cors_preflight.question: Your API platform serves 50+ APIs consumed by first-party SPAs, third-party widgets, and mobile apps. Design a tiered CORS policy architecture: define different Access-Control-Allow-Origin rules per API classification (public, partner, internal), how to handle credentialed vs non-credentialed requests, and preflight caching strategy.

api_fundamentals_http.http2_http3_evolut.question: Your organization is migrating from HTTP/1.1 to HTTP/2 across its API gateway layer. Analyze the trade-offs: how HTTP/2 multiplexing eliminates head-of-line blocking at the HTTP layer but introduces it at the TCP layer (motivating HTTP/3/QUIC), how HPACK compression benefits API headers, and what compatibility risks exist with older clients and proxies.

api_rest_design.resource_modeling_taxono.question: You're designing an e-commerce API with products, categories, reviews, and inventory. Model the resource hierarchy: define parent-child relationships, collection vs singleton resources, and explain when to use nested resources (/products/{id}/reviews) vs top-level resources (/reviews?product_id={id}).

api_rest_design.error_response_rfc7807.question: Your organization currently has 10 teams each returning errors in different JSON shapes. Design an RFC 7807 Problem Details standard for the organization: define the required fields (type, title, status, detail, instance), custom extension fields for your platform, and how validation errors should be structured with field-level detail.

api_rest_design.collection_pagination_st.question: Compare cursor-based vs offset-based pagination for your organization's API platform standard. For a high-traffic social feed API with frequent inserts and a low-traffic admin dashboard API, which pagination style would you mandate for each and why? Define the standard response envelope schema.
expected_answer_keywords: offset allows jumping to page N

api_rest_design.hateoas_maturity_model.question: Evaluate the Richardson Maturity Model levels (0-3) and recommend which level your organization's public APIs should target. Specifically, argue the trade-offs of Level 3 HATEOAS (hypermedia-driven navigation) versus Level 2 (proper HTTP verbs + status codes) considering developer experience, client complexity, and API discoverability.

api_rest_design.query_language_standards.question: Multiple teams are implementing filtering differently: Team A uses ?filter=name:eq:John, Team B uses ?name=John&age_gt=25, Team C uses ?q={"name": "John"}. Design a unified query language standard for the organization covering filtering operators, sorting syntax, and field selection (sparse fieldsets).

api_rest_design.bulk_batch_operations.question: An API consumer needs to create 500 products in a single request instead of 500 individual POST calls. Design a bulk operations standard: define the request/response format, partial success handling (some items fail, others succeed), and whether to use a synchronous response or an async job pattern with polling.

api_rest_design.api_style_guide_authorin.question: You're tasked with authoring the organization's first API style guide covering 200+ microservices across 15 teams. Outline the key sections, explain how you would enforce adoption (automated linting vs manual review), and describe how to handle teams that have legacy APIs violating the new standards.
expected_answer_keywords: style guide sections: naming, versioning, errors, auth, pagination

api_rest_design.schema_evolution_compati.question: An API needs to rename a response field from 'userName' to 'display_name' and change a required field to optional. Define the schema evolution compatibility rules for your organization: what constitutes a breaking vs non-breaking change, and how to use OpenAPI schema diff tools to automate compatibility checks in CI.
expected_answer_keywords: breaking: field removal, type change, required addition
non-breaking: field addition, required to optional

api_rest_design.hypermedia_controls.question: Design a hypermedia control standard for your organization's APIs using HAL or JSON:API link relations. Explain how _links with rel types (self, next, prev, related) enable client-driven workflow navigation, and argue when hypermedia controls add value versus when they add unnecessary complexity.

api_alternative_styles.graphql_schema_go.question: A team proposes a GraphQL schema with a generic 'data' field returning JSON blobs, queries accepting 50+ arguments, and no input validation. As the API designer, identify the schema governance violations and propose schema design rules for your organization's GraphQL API standard.

api_alternative_styles.json_rpc_specific.question: Compare JSON-RPC 2.0 with REST for an internal calculator service with operations like add(a, b), multiply(a, b), and factorial(n). Explain when JSON-RPC's method-oriented approach is more appropriate than REST's resource-oriented approach, and what the organization's selection criteria should be.
expected_answer_keywords: selection criteria: resource vs operation nature

api_alternative_styles.websocket_api_pat.question: Your organization needs real-time notifications for an order tracking system. Design a WebSocket API contract standard: define the connection handshake, message format (JSON envelope with type/payload), heartbeat/ping-pong requirements, and reconnection policies for the organization.
expected_answer_keywords: JSON message envelope: type, payload, timestamp

api_alternative_styles.grpc_service_cont.question: Your organization has 30 microservices communicating via REST, but latency-sensitive services need lower overhead. Design gRPC service contract governance: Protobuf style guide rules, .proto file organization standards, backward compatibility rules for proto field numbering, and the migration strategy from REST to gRPC for internal APIs.
expected_answer_keywords: REST gateway for external, gRPC for internal

api_alternative_styles.asyncapi_event_sp.question: Your organization publishes events from 20 microservices via Kafka but has no event schema standard. Introduce AsyncAPI specifications: define the event schema governance process, CloudEvents envelope standard, event versioning rules, and how teams should register their event contracts in a central catalog.

api_alternative_styles.api_protocol_sele.question: A new product requires three API capabilities: a public storefront (browsed by web/mobile), real-time chat between users, and high-throughput internal data pipeline between services. Define which protocol (REST, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, AsyncAPI/Kafka) you would select for each and create a protocol selection decision matrix for the organization.
expected_answer_keywords: decision matrix: latency, payload, consumer type, tooling

api_alternative_styles.federation_compos.question: Your organization has 8 teams each owning GraphQL subgraphs that need to compose into a unified supergraph (Apollo Federation). Design the federation governance: schema ownership boundaries, entity resolution standards (@key directives), composition CI checks, and how to handle breaking changes in one subgraph that affect the supergraph.

api_alternative_styles.schema_registry_m.question: Your organization uses Confluent Schema Registry for Avro event schemas but is experiencing schema compatibility failures and schema sprawl (300+ schemas, many unused). Design a schema registry governance program: compatibility mode policies (BACKWARD, FORWARD, FULL), schema lifecycle management, cleanup procedures, and team accountability.

api_alternative_styles.streaming_api_pat.question: Compare Server-Sent Events (SSE), WebSocket, gRPC server streaming, and HTTP/2 push for a real-time analytics dashboard that displays live metrics to 10,000 concurrent users. Evaluate each option's scalability, browser compatibility, reconnection handling, and infrastructure requirements, then recommend a standard.

api_auth_security.auth_scheme_selection.question: Your API platform serves three consumer types: first-party mobile apps, third-party developer integrations, and machine-to-machine internal services. Compare Bearer tokens (OAuth2), API keys, and mTLS certificates for each consumer type and recommend which auth scheme to mandate for each in the organization's API security standard.
expected_answer_keywords: API keys: simple but less secure

api_auth_security.api_key_management_pol.question: A third-party developer's API key is exposed in a public GitHub commit. Define the incident response procedure and design an API key management policy covering: key rotation cadence, automatic key expiration, environment scoping (production vs sandbox), and the developer portal key management UX.

api_auth_security.security_scheme_docume.question: Review an OpenAPI specification that has no securitySchemes defined, returns generic 'error' messages for auth failures, and uses query parameter ?token=xxx for authentication. Identify the security documentation violations and rewrite the security section following best practices.
expected_answer_keywords: securitySchemes with type: http, scheme: bearer
no tokens in query params (URL logging risk)

api_auth_security.oauth2_api_contract_pa.question: Your API platform needs to support: (1) a React SPA accessing user data, (2) a CLI tool for developers, and (3) IoT devices with limited input capability. Select the appropriate OAuth2 grant type for each, explain why PKCE is mandatory for the SPA, and define the token endpoint contract with required/optional parameters.
expected_answer_keywords: token endpoint: grant_type, code, redirect_uri, code_verifier

api_auth_security.scope_permission_model.question: Your organization has 50 APIs and each team defines scopes independently, resulting in inconsistent naming (user.read vs read_users vs users:read) and scope explosion (200+ scopes). Design a unified scope naming convention, hierarchy model, and governance process for scope creation across the organization.
expected_answer_keywords: hierarchical scopes: users:* includes users:read, users:write

api_auth_security.token_exchange_delegat.question: Service A receives a user's access token and needs to call Service B on behalf of the user, but with reduced permissions. Design a token exchange flow using RFC 8693: specify the token exchange endpoint contract, how audience restriction limits token scope, and how to prevent token replay across services.

api_auth_security.api_threat_modeling.question: Conduct an API threat modeling exercise for a banking API platform using OWASP API Security Top 10. Identify the top 3 API-specific threats (BOLA, Broken Authentication, Excessive Data Exposure) and design contract-level mitigations — not code-level fixes, but API design constraints that prevent these vulnerabilities by construction.
expected_answer_keywords: Broken Auth: mandatory auth scheme per endpoint
Excessive Data Exposure: field-level response filtering

api_auth_security.zero_trust_api_archite.question: Design a zero-trust API architecture for a microservices platform where no service trusts any other service by default. Specify mTLS requirements for service-to-service API calls, SPIFFE identity standards, token validation at every hop (not just the gateway), and the trade-offs of per-request verification vs session-based trust caching.

api_auth_security.api_abuse_prevention_d.question: Your public API is experiencing credential stuffing attacks on POST /auth/login and account enumeration via timing differences in POST /users/forgot-password. Design API contract-level defenses — not WAF rules, but API design decisions that make these attacks structurally impossible or impractical.
expected_answer_keywords: constant-time responses regardless of user existence
identical error messages for valid/invalid users
rate limiting per IP and credential pair
login endpoint returns same response shape
no user enumeration via error differences

api_performance_scalability.rate_limitin.question: Design a three-tier API quota policy (Free: 100 req/min, Pro: 1000 req/min, Enterprise: 10000 req/min) for your developer platform. Specify the RateLimit-* response headers (RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset), the 429 error response body format, and how quota resets should work (fixed window vs sliding window).
expected_answer_keywords: fixed window vs sliding window trade-off

api_performance_scalability.pagination_c.question: A team implements pagination with ?page=5&per_page=100 but their dataset has 10 million rows with frequent inserts. Users report seeing duplicate items when paginating. Explain the root cause and design a cursor-based pagination standard with the response envelope schema including cursor tokens, has_more flag, and page size limits.
expected_answer_keywords: offset pagination: row shifts on insert cause duplicates

api_performance_scalability.payload_opti.question: An API endpoint returning user profiles sends 50 fields per user when mobile clients only need 5 fields (name, avatar, status). Design a sparse fieldsets standard using a ?fields= query parameter: define the syntax, nested field selection, and how the API should respond when a requested field doesn't exist.

api_performance_scalability.caching_stra.question: Design a multi-layer caching architecture for an API platform: (1) Client-side cache via Cache-Control headers, (2) CDN edge cache for public endpoints, (3) API gateway shared cache, and (4) Application-level Redis cache. Define cache key strategies, TTL policies per layer, and how to handle cache invalidation when underlying data changes.

api_performance_scalability.api_latency_.question: Your API platform SLO requires p99 latency under 200ms for Tier 1 APIs. An API endpoint calls 3 downstream services sequentially (auth: 20ms, database: 50ms, recommendations: 80ms). Calculate the remaining latency budget, explain why this architecture risks SLO violations, and propose optimizations (parallelization, caching, timeout budgets).
expected_answer_keywords: SLO violation risk from tail latency

api_performance_scalability.connection_m.question: Compare HTTP/1.1 connection pooling (6 parallel connections per host) with HTTP/2 single-connection multiplexing for an API gateway serving 10,000 concurrent requests. Explain how HTTP/2 eliminates connection overhead but introduces stream-level flow control considerations, and define connection management policies for your API platform.

api_performance_scalability.cdn_edge_dis.question: Your API platform serves a global audience with 50ms p99 latency SLO. Design a CDN edge distribution architecture: which API responses can be edge-cached (public catalog vs personalized), how to handle cache personalization (Vary header vs edge compute), and how to manage cache consistency across 50+ edge locations during a product price change.

api_performance_scalability.capacity_pla.question: Your API platform normally handles 5,000 RPS but expects 50,000 RPS during Black Friday (10x spike). Build a capacity planning model: define the load testing approach (shadow traffic vs synthetic), auto-scaling policies (CPU/RPS-based), pre-provisioning strategy, and how to implement graceful degradation when capacity is exceeded.

api_performance_scalability.throttling_b.question: Your streaming API pushes events to consumers at varying rates. Fast producers overwhelm slow consumers causing memory pressure and dropped events. Design a backpressure signaling standard for your API platform: compare reactive pull-based flow control, token-based rate negotiation, and HTTP 429 with Retry-After for REST-based throttling.

api_integration_patterns.webhook_design_.question: A team implements webhooks that: (1) send raw database records as payloads, (2) have no event type field, (3) retry infinitely on failure, and (4) provide no signature verification. Design a webhook contract standard fixing all issues: define the event envelope schema, HMAC signature verification, retry policy with exponential backoff, and dead-letter handling.
expected_answer_keywords: event envelope: type, id, timestamp, data

api_integration_patterns.api_mocking_vir.question: A frontend team is blocked because the backend API isn't ready yet. Design an API mocking standard for your organization: select a mocking tool (Prism, WireMock, MockServer), define how mocks should be generated from OpenAPI specs, how to maintain mock fidelity with the real API, and how to integrate mocks into the developer onboarding flow.
expected_answer_keywords: mock fidelity: regenerate on spec change

api_integration_patterns.sdk_client_gene.question: Your API platform supports 4 programming languages (JavaScript, Python, Java, Go). Design an SDK generation pipeline from OpenAPI specifications: select the generation tool (openapi-generator), define how SDK versioning aligns with API versioning, and establish SDK quality standards (generated code must include error handling, retries, and pagination helpers).

api_integration_patterns.event_driven_ap.question: Compare three event-driven API patterns: (1) Webhooks (HTTP push), (2) Server-Sent Events (SSE streaming), and (3) AsyncAPI over Kafka. For an order management system that needs to notify warehouse, payment, and shipping services, evaluate each pattern's delivery guarantees, consumer complexity, and scaling characteristics.

api_integration_patterns.contract_testin.question: Your organization has 30 microservices with REST API dependencies but no contract testing. Introduce Pact contract testing governance: define the consumer-driven workflow (consumer writes pact → provider verifies), CI/CD integration with Pact Broker, and how to handle the 'provider changed without checking consumers' failure mode.

api_integration_patterns.consumer_driven.question: Service A (provider) has 5 consumer services, each using different subsets of the response schema. Consumer C only uses {id, name, status} but the full response has 30 fields. Explain how consumer-driven contracts prevent Provider from breaking Consumer C's expectations, and design the governance workflow when Provider needs to rename the 'status' field.
expected_answer_keywords: provider validates against all consumer contracts
field rename = breaking for Consumer C
migration plan: add new field, notify consumers, update contracts, remove old field

api_integration_patterns.api_gateway_arc.question: Your organization needs an API gateway strategy supporting: public APIs (rate limited, OAuth2), partner APIs (API key, custom SLAs), and internal APIs (mTLS, no rate limiting). Compare single gateway with multi-tiered routing vs separate gateway instances per API classification. Evaluate Kong vs Apigee vs AWS API Gateway for this multi-tenant architecture.
expected_answer_keywords: cross-cutting concerns: logging, auth, rate limiting

api_integration_patterns.service_mesh_ap.question: Your organization is rolling out Istio service mesh for internal API routing. Design the traffic management strategy: how to implement canary releases (route 5% of API traffic to v2), header-based routing for A/B testing (X-Feature-Flag: new-checkout), and circuit breaker policies at the mesh level instead of application code.

api_integration_patterns.backward_compat.question: A team deployed an API change that removed a response field, breaking 3 consumer services in production. Design an automated backward compatibility testing system: how to detect breaking changes from OpenAPI spec diffs, integrate checks into CI/CD as a blocking gate, and handle legitimate breaking changes with a deprecation-first workflow.
expected_answer_keywords: deprecation-first: mark deprecated → sunset period → remove

api_lifecycle_governance.api_versioning_.question: Compare three API versioning approaches for your organization's standard: URI path versioning (/v1/users), header versioning (API-Version: 2), and media type versioning (Accept: application/vnd.company.v2+json). Evaluate each approach's developer experience, cacheability, and routing complexity, then recommend one as the organization default.
expected_answer_keywords: URI path: simple, cacheable, URL pollution
URI path most common and DX-friendly

api_lifecycle_governance.api_documentati.question: Review an API documentation page that has: (1) no authentication section, (2) no error response examples, (3) a single curl command as the only code sample, and (4) no rate limiting information. Define the minimum required sections for your organization's API documentation standard and explain why each section is critical for developer adoption.
expected_answer_keywords: required sections: overview, auth, endpoints, errors, rate limits, code samples
error response examples for each status code

api_lifecycle_governance.api_changelog_c.question: Your API platform releases weekly updates but consumers complain about surprise breaking changes. Design a changelog communication standard: define the changelog format (Keep a Changelog structure), breaking change notification workflow (email + portal banner + Sunset header), and the minimum advance notice period before breaking changes take effect.
expected_answer_keywords: Keep a Changelog format: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed
breaking change advance notice (90 days minimum)

api_lifecycle_governance.deprecation_sun.question: Your organization needs to sunset API v1 (released 3 years ago) used by 200+ consumers while migrating them to v2. Design the deprecation lifecycle: define the sunset timeline (announcement → deprecation period → traffic monitoring → sunset), Sunset header (RFC 8594) implementation, consumer migration support, and the decision criteria for extending the sunset date.
expected_answer_keywords: sunset timeline: announce → deprecate → monitor → sunset
extension criteria: high-traffic consumers not migrated

api_lifecycle_governance.api_catalog_dis.question: Your organization has 200+ APIs across 20 teams but no central catalog — developers discover APIs via Slack messages and tribal knowledge. Design an API catalog system using Backstage: define the required metadata per API entry (owner, lifecycle status, documentation link, SLA tier), the registration workflow, and how to enforce catalog completeness.
expected_answer_keywords: required metadata: owner, lifecycle, docs, SLA
CI check: API must have catalog entry

api_lifecycle_governance.design_review_p.question: Your organization has no API design review process, and teams ship APIs with inconsistent naming, authentication, and error formats. Design the API design review workflow: define the review checklist (naming, versioning, auth, errors, pagination), the review board composition, how to use Spectral linting for automated pre-review checks, and the approval/rejection process.
expected_answer_keywords: review checklist: naming, versioning, auth, errors, pagination
Spectral linting in CI as pre-filter

api_lifecycle_governance.developer_porta.question: Your developer portal has a 30-minute time-to-first-API-call for new developers, and adoption surveys show frustration with API key provisioning and lack of interactive documentation. Design improvements: specify the ideal onboarding flow (sign up → get API key → try API in playground → integrate), interactive Try-It features, and how to measure developer satisfaction (TTFC, CSAT).

api_lifecycle_governance.api_metrics_ana.question: Your API platform has 200+ APIs but no visibility into which APIs are thriving and which are failing. Design an API analytics framework: define the key metrics (adoption rate, error rate, latency percentiles, consumer growth, API deprecation candidates), build a health scoring model, and explain how to use data to drive API portfolio decisions (sunset, invest, or standardize).
expected_answer_keywords: key metrics: adoption, error rate, p99 latency, consumer growth
portfolio quadrant: invest, sunset, standardize, experiment

api_lifecycle_governance.compliance_regu.question: Your banking API platform must comply with GDPR (data minimization in responses), PCI DSS (card data masking), and PSD2 (Open Banking API standards). Design API contract-level compliance controls: how to enforce data minimization in response schemas, field-level masking rules, audit trail requirements in API contracts, and PSD2 mandatory endpoint specifications.
expected_answer_keywords: GDPR: minimal response fields, purpose limitation
PCI DSS: mask card numbers in responses

api_lifecycle_governance.api_program_man.question: Your CTO asks you to establish an API Program Office to transform the organization into an API-first company. Design the program: define the governance council structure (representatives from each engineering team), API maturity model (levels 1-5), success metrics (time-to-integration, API reuse rate, developer satisfaction), and how to align API strategy with business revenue goals.
expected_answer_keywords: success metrics: TTI, reuse rate, developer satisfaction
